I’ve been having a hard time since… well, it’s been a few weeks now, maybe less than a month? It’s hard to keep track. Working in hospice, I’ve seen a lot, but one of the patients’ passing hit differently this time. I can’t shake it. Some nights I sleep for eight hours, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all—drained, heavy, like my body didn’t rest.  

And then, out of nowhere, I’ll be at work changing linens or giving meds, and suddenly I’m back there—seeing her face, hearing the monitor flatline, feeling that same knot in my chest. It’s not like a memory; it’s like it’s happening again. I freeze for a second, and then I’m back. It’s brief, but terrifying.  

I don’t know how long this has been going on. A couple of weeks? Maybe three weeks exactly—it blurs. I don’t want to talk about it much. I just keep hoping it’ll pass. I still go to work. I still do the job. But something feels… off. Like I’m not all here. I used to be able to compartmentalize, but now I just feel stranded between the living and the dying—and I don’t know where I belong.
D019-D020_h001.question_a:
I’m a hospice caregiver, so I’ve seen my share of tough moments, but nothing like what happened last week. One of my patients—someone I’d been sitting with for days—coded suddenly, and I was right there. It was chaotic, and I couldn’t help… I just froze. Since then, I can’t shake it. I keep *reliving* it—like I’m back in that room, seeing it all happen again, sometimes when I’m just brushing my teeth or closing my eyes. It feels real, like it’s happening *now*. 

I’m sleeping maybe six hours a night, but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t sleep at all. My mind won't shut off. I’ve been jumpy, too—I dropped a teacup yesterday because a car honked outside. I’ve been avoiding the unit where it happened, and I can’t talk about it without feeling like I’m right back there. 

It’s only been ten days, but it’s getting worse. I’ve never felt like this before—like I’m not even myself. I don’t know how to turn it off.
D019-D020_h001.question_b:
I’ve been having a really hard time since my best friend passed away three weeks ago. She died in my arms at work—she was one of my hospice patients, and we’d become close over the months. Ever since, I keep having these moments where I feel like I’m right back there, seeing her take her last breath. It hits out of nowhere, like I’m reliving it. I wake up drenched in sweat, and even after eight hours of sleep, I feel completely drained, like I didn’t rest at all.  

It’s been hard to focus at work, and I’ve started avoiding certain patients, especially those nearing the end. I know it’s part of the job, but this one got into my heart in a way I didn’t expect. I’ve never reacted like this before, even after other losses.  

It all started about ten days after she died—within that first month—but I don’t feel like I'm completely "checked out" or numb. I’m sad and anxious, yes, and the flashbacks are scary, but I don’t feel detached from reality for long stretches, and I haven’t been avoiding everything. I’m still showing up, just barely. It’s just… it hasn’t gone away like I thought it would.
